newsitem.title: USA: Forest Oil lists West Cameron production.
newsitem.headline: Forest Oil lists West Cameron production.

text.p: Forest Oil Corp said Thursday production has begun from a natural gas find on West Cameron Block 615 at the low end of the projected range.
The company said three directionally-drilled wells are flowing at a combined rate of 40 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.
Early last month, the operator of the Block 615 platform, Apache Corp, said production was expected in February at a rate of 40 to 50 million cubic feet daily.
This project is in about 300 feet of water offshore Lousiana in the Gulf of Mexico.
Apache has a 50 percent working interest, as did Forest Oil, which sold a 25 percent stake to Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc.

Subsequent to the discovery on West Cameron Block 615, Forest Oil said, it acquired a 50 percent working interest in two adjoining blocks, West Cameron Blocks 616 and 617. The other 50 percent is held by a joint venture of McMoRan Oil & Gas Co and MCN Corp.
Forest said further 3D seismic evaluations of these blocks is now being conducted. The discovery well drilled on Block 616 in 1996 was cased and temporarily abandoned in June.
Forest said it anticipates additional drilling on the blocks in the second and third quarters of 1997.

It said the A-1 discovery well on Block 615 is producing at a rate of 24 million cubic feet per day with 2,000 pounds per square inch of flowing tubing pressure from 45 feet of perforations in the 6,700 foot Pleistocene-age sand.
Its offset, the A-2, is flowing 11 million cubic feet of natural gas per day with 1,850 pounds per square ince of flowing tubing pressure from 19 feet of perforations in the same formation.

The third well on the block, the A-3, discovered natural gas in a new fault block in the 5,850 foot Pleistocene-age sand. It is producing at a daily rate of 5 million cubic feet with 1,560 pounds per square inch of flowing tubing pressure through 22 feet of perforations.
